\[
ct(u) = \int_0^u 1 + \frac{\sigma_s}{\sigma_r} \sum_{k=1}^{3} \lvert I_k'(x) \rvert \, dx
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(ct(u)\): The position of pixel u on the stretched axis
- \(\sigma_s\): The spatial sigma
- \(\sigma_r\): The color sigma
- \(I_k'\): The change of channel k between neighbors

Gastal and Oliveira map each row, or column, to a new axis ct. A step of one pixel adds 1, plus the color change between the two pixels times sigma s over sigma r. So in flat areas the new axis looks like the old one, and at an edge it jumps far. A 1-D filter of sigma s along ct then mixes pixels only when they are close on the new axis, which means close in space and in color. Rows and columns take turns, and each pass uses a smaller sigma so that the passes together smooth with sigma s. Every step is linear in the number of pixels, whatever the sigmas.
